# BioChef · full content

> A signed catalogue of bioinformatics tools that run end-to-end in your browser via WebAssembly. From a YAML recipe in Git to a signed bundle in the BioChef Registry, then executed client-side. No installs, no uploads, no servers.

This is the full-content companion to <https://home.biochef.app/llms.txt>. It inlines the prose of every public page so an LLM can ingest the whole marketing/docs site in one fetch.

The site at <https://home.biochef.app/> documents BioChef, an open project from IEETA at the University of Aveiro. The actual BioChef web app users run lives at <https://biochef.app/>; this site is the marketing/docs front door.

---

## Home (/)

**Headline:** Genomics tools in a browser tab.

An open catalogue of bioinformatics tools that run end-to-end in your browser. No installs, no uploads.

Peer-reviewed in BMC Bioinformatics, 2026. DOI: 10.1186/s12859-026-06431-1.

### Platform pillars (what you get)

- **Recipes → Hub → Registry.** Tools are declared as YAML recipes, validated and built by biochef-hub (SBOM, SLSA, cosign), then published as signed bundles to the BioChef Registry.
- **Browser-native WebAssembly.** Every published tool runs client-side in WebAssembly. Open the BioChef app, drop in a sequence, and execute. No installs, no uploads, no servers.
- **Drag-and-drop DAGs.** A DAG editor chains tools end-to-end. Tools are filtered by data type, parameters re-execute live, and workflows can be exported and shared as JSON.

### Architecture at a glance

A YAML recipe in Git, signed by the Hub CI, served from the BioChef Registry, and run as WebAssembly in your browser. Four stations: Recipes (orange) → Hub (teal) → Registry (dark teal) → Browser (blue). Every artifact is content-addressable; every step is signed.

### Ecosystem fit

- **WebAssembly runtime.** Bioinformatics tools compiled with Emscripten and biowasm; everything runs in the browser.
- **OCI Registry distribution.** Signed bundles published to `registry.biochef.app` with SBOM and SLSA provenance.
- **Sigstore cosign provenance.** Every recipe is built, tested, signed, and an immutable digest is recorded in the signed `index.json`.

---

## Why BioChef (/why)

**Headline:** Why BioChef.

BioChef democratizes access to bioinformatics tools, bridging biologists, healthcare professionals, and computational tools by running compiled bioinformatics utilities directly in the browser via WebAssembly.

Designed for: researchers, clinicians, students.
Privacy model: no upload, no server, no install.
Source of trust: signed bundles in the Registry.

### The case: a tool every reviewer can re-run

**The problem — tools are hard to share and trust.** Most bioinformatics tools require local installs, native toolchains, and trust in opaque container images. End users like clinicians, students, and reviewers can't easily inspect or run them, and reproducibility suffers.

**The solution — Recipe → Hub → Registry → browser.** A YAML recipe declares the tool. `biochef-hub` validates, builds (WASM via Emscripten/biowasm), tests, generates SBOM + SLSA, signs with cosign, and publishes a signed bundle to `registry.biochef.app`. The static BioChef web app then loads it by digest and runs it client-side. No servers, no uploads.

### Use cases

- **Standardize sequence analysis (researchers).** Run signed tools for FASTA/FASTQ manipulation, format conversion, and statistics with reproducible parameters.
- **No installs, nothing uploaded (privacy).** The whole BioChef app is a static page. Tools are compiled to WebAssembly and execute on your sequence inside the browser tab.
- **Build and share workflows (workflow authors).** Drag tools into a DAG, configure parameters, and re-run live as you iterate. Export the workflow and import it again in one click.

### Traditional toolchain vs BioChef

| Aspect | Traditional toolchain | With BioChef |
|---|---|---|
| Tool provenance | Opaque containers, ad-hoc signing | Signed recipes → Hub → Registry with SBOM and SLSA |
| Getting started | Install toolchain, build from source, manage dependencies | Open the BioChef app in a browser tab |
| Data handling | Upload sequences to a server you have to trust | WASM execution keeps every byte inside the browser tab |
| Iterating on a workflow | Edit shell script, re-run, hope for reproducibility | DAG editor with live re-execution; every tool in it comes from the signed catalogue |
| Sharing a result | Send a tarball plus a README | Share the workflow file. Anyone can import and re-run it in the app |

---

## Architecture (/architecture)

**Headline:** Anatomy of a BioChef tool.

Four pieces ship today: YAML recipes in Git, the Hub CI that signs and publishes, the BioChef Registry, and the static web app that runs every tool as WebAssembly in your browser.

Live components: Recipes · Hub · Registry · Web app.
Build chain: Emscripten · biowasm · cosign.
Distribution: `registry.biochef.app`.

### The path a tool travels (four stations, left to right)

**01 · Source — biochef-recipes.** YAML source of truth. Each tool is a `biochef.yaml` file declaring inputs, runtime, and version. → push.

**02 · Build — biochef-hub.** CI on GitHub Actions: validate, build to WASM or native, test on example inputs, generate SBOM and SLSA, sign with cosign. → publish (ORAS · cosign).

**03 · Distribute — BioChef Registry.** Content-addressable OCI bundles at `registry.biochef.app`: `bundle.json`, WASM/JS layers, SBOM, signature. → fetch by digest (dashed = runtime).

**04 · Runtime — BioChef web app.** Static SPA fetches tools by digest, verifies the signature, and runs them as WebAssembly inside your browser tab.

Every artifact is content-addressable · every step is signed.

### Component details

**Recipes & Hub.** Recipes declare tools/workflows; Hub validates, signs, and bundles them for Registry. Schema validation against the BioChef recipe schema; each built tool is run on the example input of its data types. Builds with Emscripten/biowasm (WASM) or as a native tarball; generates SBOM and SLSA attestation. Pushes the bundle to the BioChef Registry, signs it with keyless cosign and attaches SLSA provenance, then republishes the signed `index.json` catalogue. Author YAML in `biochef-recipes` under `recipes/<tool>/biochef.yaml`; validate before opening a PR. Keep inputs/outputs typed; CI runs each tool on the example input of its data types. The reusable workflows live in `biochef-hub/.github/workflows/validate-recipes.yml` (PR validation) and `publish-recipes.yml` (build + publish on merge).

**Registry & Catalog.** The BioChef Registry, live at `registry.biochef.app`, stores signed OCI artifacts (`bundle.json` + WASM/JS layers + SBOM) and the signed `index.json` that lists every published tool by digest. Each tool version is content-addressable: pulled by digest, not by mutable tag. The Hub signs every bundle with keyless cosign, and signs the top-level `index.json` catalogue (ES256) only after verifying those signatures and the SLSA provenance. WASM and JS assets are served as plain HTTPS so the browser app can stream them. Treat each version as immutable; promote new builds, never overwrite digests. The browser checks the catalogue signature and every digest itself before running a tool; cosign and SLSA are verified by the Hub before the catalogue is signed. Use the signed `index.json` as the source of truth for what is publishable.

**UI & WASM Runtime.** The BioChef web app, a static React/Webpack SPA, runs every published bioinformatics tool entirely in the browser via WebAssembly. Has a Tools page for single-tool runs and a Workflow page for DAG-style chains. Loads tools by digest from the BioChef Registry; aioli/biowasm boots them in a Web Worker. Before showing any tool, the app checks the catalogue's signature against a public key pinned in the app and keeps only entries that passed the publication checks; before running one, it checks the SHA-256 of the OCI manifest, the bundle, the JavaScript and the WebAssembly. A tool that fails is not offered. Detects input data type (FASTA, FASTQ, Multi-FASTA, DNA, RNA, amino acids, BAM, SAM, CRAM, VCF, BCF, BED, GFF, JSON, LIST, …) and filters compatible tools. DAG editor re-executes downstream steps on parameter change; workflows can be exported and imported as JSON. The SPA's bundled GTO modules are built with Emscripten 3.1.65 (rebuild locally with `npm run build-wasm`); Hub CI compiles new recipes with Emscripten 4.0.18. Outputs stream live to the Output panel; inspect intermediate steps without re-running the whole pipeline. The whole app is static. Host it from any CDN or GitHub Pages.

---

## Workflows (/workflows)

**Headline:** Build workflows.

Drag bioinformatics tools into a DAG inside your browser tab. Outputs flow live, parameters re-execute on the fly, and the whole thing is just a static page that runs WebAssembly.

Editor: drag-and-drop DAG with type filtering.
Runtime: WebAssembly via biowasm.
Persistence: workflows exported as JSON.

### Editor preview (drag, drop, watch outputs flow)

A four-node sketch of what the Workflow page looks like in the BioChef app. Click a node to see what feeds it and what it produces. Default WASM pipeline today: input FASTQ → gto.fastq.info / gto.fastq.to.fasta → gto.fasta.reverse → output.

### Example scenarios

- **Sequencing data triage.** Run fastp for QC and adapter trimming, then chain samtools view/stats/flagstat or GTO statistics to triage FASTQ or BAM/CRAM in seconds, no upload needed.
- **Format conversion pipeline (data prep).** Convert between FASTA, FASTQ, SEQ, BAM ↔ SAM (samtools), GTF ↔ GFF (gffread); reverse, complement, slice. All in one workflow.
- **Teaching demo (education).** Send a workflow file to a class. Anyone can import it in the browser and walk through the same DAG step by step.

### Tool catalogue snapshot

- GTO suite (57+ ops): sequence · format · genomic · amino acid · info · text
- Alignment & mapping (6): minimap2 · lastz · mummer4/nucmer · ssw · ksw2 · edlib
- Variants & consensus (3): bcftools · ivar · viralconsensus
- BAM/SAM & QC (3): samtools view/sort/stats · fastp · samblaster
- MSA & phylogenetics (6): muscle · kalign · abPOA · fasttree · ASTER · tn93
- Genome intervals (2): bedtools intersect · cgranges coverage
- Assembly, ORFs & methylation (3): fermi-lite assemble · prodigal · modbam2bed
- Sequence toolkits (2): seqtk · gffread — subseq · convert · filter
- Text, JSON & shell (5): gawk · grep · sed · jq · coreutils
- And growing: new recipes added by the community

Counts approximate. Workflows can pipe FASTA, FASTQ, BAM, SAM, CRAM, VCF, BCF, BED, GFF, JSON, LIST and more between tools.

### How execution works (one runtime today)

Every step runs in the browser via WebAssembly. Server-side runtimes are on the roadmap.

Live runtime — Browser WebAssembly. Every shipped tool runs entirely in your browser tab. No upload, no install, no server. Where: your browser tab. Compiled with: Emscripten · biowasm. Loaded by: signed digest from registry.

---

## Developers (/developers)

**Headline:** For Developers.

Write a YAML recipe, push it through the Hub CI, and your tool ends up signed in `registry.biochef.app` and runnable from the BioChef web app.

Hub CLI: Python, reusable GitHub workflow.
Recipes: `biochef.yaml` in Git.
Local dev: clone the SPA, `npm start`.

### Three ways in (pick a path, get to a running BioChef in under five minutes)

**Step 01 · Author — write a new recipe.** Author a YAML recipe in your own repo. The Hub workflow validates, signs, and publishes it for you.
1. Fork `biochef-recipes` and create `recipes/<tool>/biochef.yaml`.
2. Run `hub validate` on it. CI also runs each built tool on the example input of its data types, so declare the types carefully.
3. Open a PR. The reusable Hub workflow runs validate → build → test → SBOM. After merge it publishes, signs with cosign, attaches SLSA provenance and republishes the signed catalogue.
Recipes repo: <https://github.com/ieeta-pt/biochef-recipes> · Hub CI: <https://github.com/ieeta-pt/biochef-hub>

**Step 02 · Run — run the BioChef app locally.** Clone the SPA, install deps, and serve it with the dev server. No backend required.
1. `git clone https://github.com/ieeta-pt/Biochef` and `npm install`.
2. (Optional) install Emscripten 3.1.65 and run `npm run build-wasm` to rebuild WASM modules from source.
3. `npm start` and open `http://localhost:8082`.

**Step 03 · Inspect — pull a signed bundle.** Tools live in the BioChef Registry as content-addressable OCI bundles. The web app fetches them by digest at runtime; you can pull them with ORAS and verify them with cosign.
1. Resolve a tool by digest in the signed `index.json` catalogue.
2. Pull the OCI bundle (`bundle.json` + WASM/JS layers + SBOM) with ORAS.
3. Verify the bundle's cosign signature and SLSA provenance; the web app itself checks the catalogue signature and every digest before running it.
Hub CLI on GitHub: <https://github.com/ieeta-pt/biochef-hub>

### Snippets (what the code looks like)

A recipe in YAML, the Hub CLI run, and an exported workflow.

**YAML recipe:**
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
id: app.biochef.wgsim
name: wgsim
description: Simulate NGS reads from a reference FASTA.
version: 0.3.1-bc.1
homepage: https://github.com/lh3/wgsim
license:
  spdx: MIT
  files: [wgsim.c]
maintainers:
  - name: Biochef
source:
  repo: https://github.com/lh3/wgsim
  commit: "a12da3375ff3b51a5594d4b6fa35591173ecc229"
  version: "0.3.1"
status: experimental
build:
  wasm:
    strategy: emscripten
    emscripten:
      emscriptenVersion: 4.0.18
      buildScript: build-wasm.sh
  native:
    buildScript: build-native.sh
    buildTools: [gcc]
runtime:
  modes: [wasm, native]
operations:
  - id: wgsim.simulate
    name: Simulate (wgsim)
    category: Genomic Operations
    bin: wgsim
    description: Simulate paired-end reads
    io:
      inputs:
        - { name: ref, types: [FASTA], mode: file }
      outputs:
        - { name: out1, types: [FASTQ], mode: file, flag: "", filename: "read1.fq" }
        - { name: out2, types: [FASTQ], mode: file, flag: "", filename: "read2.fq" }
    parameters:
      - { name: num_pairs, type: integer, flag: -N }
      - { name: seed, type: integer, flag: -S }
```

**CLI usage:**
```bash
# On every pull request
$ python hub/hub.py validate recipes/wgsim/biochef.yaml
$ python hub/hub.py build
$ python hub/hub.py test
$ python hub/hub.py sbom && python hub/hub.py sbom-check

# After merge, in CI only (keyless cosign, SLSA, signed catalogue)
$ python hub/hub.py publish --registry registry.biochef.app
$ python hub/hub.py sign-attest --policy … --expected-hub-commit …
$ python hub/hub.py verify-attestations --policy … --expected-hub-commit …
$ python hub/hub.py publish-catalog --registry registry.biochef.app --policy … --slsa-verification-report …
```

**Workflow JSON:**
```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "in",  "type": "inputWorkflowNode",  "position": { "x": 50,  "y": 120 }, "data": { "label": "Input" } },
    { "id": "rev", "type": "workflowNode",       "position": { "x": 350, "y": 120 }, "data": { "label": "Fasta Reverse (GTO)", "paramValues": {} } },
    { "id": "out", "type": "outputWorkflowNode", "position": { "x": 650, "y": 120 }, "data": { "label": "Output" } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "id": "e1", "type": "workflowEdge", "source": "in",  "sourceHandle": "out", "target": "rev", "targetHandle": "in" },
    { "id": "e2", "type": "workflowEdge", "source": "rev", "sourceHandle": "out", "target": "out" }
  ],
  "viewport": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "zoom": 1 }
}
```

## Community & Roadmap (/community)

**Headline:** Community & Roadmap.

Track project progress, explore what is coming next, and meet the team behind BioChef.

Live since: 2024 (web app) · 2025 (Hub).
Built by: IEETA · University of Aveiro.
License: MIT (code) · CC-BY 4.0 (paper).

### Project status

The web app, Hub CI, and Registry are live today. Agent mode and workflow aggregation are in active development. Federated learning is on the longer roadmap.

- **Live — BioChef web app.** Tools page + Workflow page; bioinformatics tools (GTO, minimap2, samtools, bcftools, bedtools, seqtk, muscle, kalign, fasttree, ivar, prodigal, mummer4, fastp, and more) running in WebAssembly via biowasm.
- **Live — biochef-hub + Registry.** Reusable GitHub workflow signs and publishes recipes to `registry.biochef.app`.
- **In development — Agent mode & workflow aggregation.** BioChef Agent runs signed bundles outside the browser, next to the data. Already working: every step runs in a container; a bundle is refused unless its signature, SBOM, SLSA provenance and blob digests check out; requests are authenticated; runs can be stopped and outlive the request; logs stream live; large files stream instead of being held in memory; each run records how it was produced. Workflow aggregation comes next.

### Roadmap

- BioChef web app: Tools + Workflow pages [done]. A growing catalogue of bioinformatics tools (GTO, minimap2, samtools, bcftools, bedtools, seqtk, muscle, kalign, fasttree, ivar, prodigal, mummer4, fastp, and more) compiled to WebAssembly, in-browser DAG editor, workflow export and import. Live at biochef.app.
- biochef-hub CI + signed Registry [done]. Reusable GitHub workflow that validates, builds and tests recipes, generates and checks an SBOM, publishes bundles to registry.biochef.app, signs them with cosign, attaches SLSA provenance, and publishes a signed catalogue that the web app verifies.
- biochef-recipes catalog growth [in progress]. Expand the public recipe catalogue with more tools, more contributors, and richer metadata. 12 of the 31 recipes also build natively, so the agent can run them outside the browser.
- Agent mode [in progress]. Runtime that executes signed bundles outside the browser, next to the data, with the same provenance guarantees. Working today: containerised steps, refusal of any bundle whose signature, SBOM, SLSA provenance or blob digests do not check out, authenticated requests, stoppable runs, live logs, streamed large files and a provenance record per run.
- Workflow aggregation [planned]. Package multi-step workflows as first-class signed artifacts in the registry, alongside individual tools, so a whole pipeline becomes a single shareable recipe.
- GA4GH standards and audit in the agent [in progress]. The agent speaks GA4GH: runs submitted through the WES API, researchers identified by GA4GH Passports, data fetched by DRS URI from hosts named in advance, plus an audit log of who ran what over which data. Implemented and in review.
- Federated learning + server runtimes [planned]. Federated Aggregator + Silo Agents, TES, htsget/refget connectors, MCP gateway, observability. Designed, not yet built.
